snp3.3:1.2: I have heard that on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
snp3.3:1.5: “Yes, lord,” the monks responded to him.
snp3.3:2.1: “Monks, speech endowed with four characteristics is well-spoken, not poorly spoken—faultless & not to be faulted by the observant.
snp3.3:2.3: There is the case where a monk says only what is well-spoken, not what is poorly spoken; only what is just, not what is unjust; only what is endearing, not what is unendearing; only what is true, not what is false.
snp3.3:2.4: Speech endowed with these four characteristics is well-spoken, not poorly spoken—faultless & not to be faulted by the observant.”
snp3.3:2.5: That is what the Blessed One said.
snp3.3:2.6: Having said this, the One Well-Gone, the Teacher, said further:
snp3.3:3.1: The calm say that what is well-spoken is best;
snp3.3:3.2:
second, that one should say
what is just, not unjust;
snp3.3:3.4: fourth, what is true, not false.
snp3.3:4.1: Then Ven. Vaṅgīsa, rising from his seat, arranging his robe over one shoulder, faced the Blessed One with his hands palm-to-palm in front of his heart and said,
snp3.3:4.2: “An inspiration has come to me, Blessed One! An inspiration has come to me, One Well-Gone!”
snp3.3:4.3: “Let the inspiration come to you, Vaṅgīsa,” the Blessed One said.
snp3.3:4.4: Then Ven. Vaṅgīsa praised the Blessed One to his face with these fitting verses:
snp3.3:6.4:
Speech when it brings no evil
to others
is pleasant.
snp3.3:7.3:
The goal and the Dhamma
—so say the calm—
snp3.3:8.1: The speech the Awakened One speaks,
snp3.3:8.3:
for making an end
to the mass of stress:
